**Additional Requirements for Application to TTU K-12**

When applying to the Texas Tech K-12 programs, you will need to meet the following requirements in addition to submitting the application form:

- **Webcam and Microphone**: A working webcam and microphone are necessary for online activities and assessments.

For more information or assistance, you can contact TTU K-12 at 1-800-692-6877 or email ttuk12@ttu.edu.

Online instruction presents different challenges than those in a traditional classroom. The curriculum is rigorous and is reading- and writing-intensive. Successful online students are able to take initiative and manage their own time.

Nevertheless, Texas Tech K-12 strives to offer exceptional education programs that meet the needs of students with disabilities. To qualify, the student's Individual Education Plan (IEP) needs to indicate that the Texas Tech K-12 online program is the appropriate instructional setting for the student and is the student’s least restrictive environment.

The student’s admission, review, and dismissal (ARD) committee has the responsibility of determining whether or not an electronic (online) course/program will meet the needs of a student with a disability. The committee will also take into account the nature of the asynchronous program and what services can be implemented online. It is crucial to note that the program is fully online, providing only services that can be provided virtually as the school does not have a physical location. The Admission, Review, and Dismissal committee will make an informed decision about an online program and the educational appropriateness of this academic setting for a student and his or her particular academic needs.

ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE (AI) USE POLICY (REVISED 2025)

This policy covers any generative Artificial Intelligence tool, such as Chat Generative Pre-trained Transformer, Elicit, Photo Math, etc. This includes text and artwork/graphics/video/audio, etc.

All work submitted in this course must be your own. You may not use artificial intelligence tools to complete your assignments in this course.

The instructor will message the student or provide feedback on the assignment indicating the need to schedule a one-on-one video conference, during which the student will be required to demonstrate their skills or knowledge through an alternative or mutually agreed-upon assignment. The grade of the alternate or agreed upon assignment will be determined at the instructor’s discretion with the highest possible score being 70%.

If it is determined that a student has violated final exam directions on Final Exam A or Credit By Exam Set 1, the exam will be scored as zero. The student may take Final Exam B or Credit By Exam Set 2 with the highest possible score being 70%.

Texas Tech High School Program Requirements

Texas Tech High School: As a full-time Texas Tech K-12 high school student, you must maintain academic progress in a minimum of four courses concurrently. Note: you will need to take more than the minimum number of courses to stay on grade level and graduate at your desired time.

To graduate with a Texas Tech High School diploma, you will take at least your last year of high school credits (25%) from Texas Tech K-12. Exceptions will be considered by administration on a case-by-case basis but the last semester (2.5 credits) must be taken from Texas Tech K-12.

Students demonstrate attendance in Texas Tech K-12 online school by regularly completing assignments. Attendance is directly tied to what the student accomplishes and/or produces over a given period. Texas Tech High School Program Requirements

Texas Tech High School: As a full-time Texas Tech K-12 high school student, you must maintain academic progress in a minimum of four courses concurrently. Note: you will need to take more than the minimum number of courses to stay on grade level and graduate at your desired time.

To complete and retain admission as a student in Texas Tech High School, you must work with an academic advisor and be enrolled in a minimum of four Texas Tech K-12 courses (dual-credit and Credit By Exam's excluded). Generally, you will complete a total of six to seven credits per year (12-14 courses) and must also pass five State of Texas Assessment and Academic Readiness (STAAR) EOC (End of Course) exams to meet graduation requirements.

To graduate with a Texas Tech High School diploma, you will take at least your last year of high school credits (25%) from Texas Tech K-12. Exceptions will be considered by administration on a case-by-case basis but the last semester (2.5 credits) must be taken from Texas Tech K-12.

Texas Tech K-12 High School Program - Full-Time

Texas Tech K-12 is a state-approved option for students who need or desire the flexibility of a distance education to earn their high school diploma. We offer all courses necessary to meet the requirements to complete a Texas high school graduation plan.

Can my child earn a diploma through the Full-Time Tuition-Paid Program?

Yes! Upon successful completion of the required coursework, students will receive a Texas Tech K-12 diploma. The program also offers options for credit recovery and accelerated learning, helping students meet their educational goals.

Texas Tech K-12 offers a tuition-based option for students who desire the flexibility of a distance education but reside outside of Texas or do not want the additional restrictions of the tuition-free program. We offer all courses necessary to meet the requirements to complete a Texas high school graduation plan. If you are currently a Texas Tech K-12 student or if you want to withdraw from your local school district to attend Texas Tech K-12 full-time but you do not want the additional restrictions of the tuition-free program, you will select this option. Once a student submits an assignment for grading, they are no longer eligible for a refund in the tuition-paid or supplemental programs.

College Preparatory Academy (Do not select if you do not meet the criteria listed below) (opens in new tab)

Texas Tech K-12 offers both individual dual credit courses or a comprehensive Texas Tech College Preparatory Academy program. The College Preparatory Academy is designed to help students graduate with both a high school diploma and a bachelor's degree in just six years.

In order to apply for the College Preparatory Academy, you must meet the following criteria:

Step 1: Achieved Mastered State of Texas Assessment of Academic Readiness (STAAR) scores

Step 2: Provided one academic recommendation letter

Step 3: Maintained a 3.0 GPA

Pathway to Success - Earn Credits Before Graduation

Earning dual credit in high school offers several benefits, especially through online dual credit courses like those offered by Texas Tech K-12. Students can complete their initial two years of undergraduate studies at Texas Tech K-12 before transitioning to Texas Tech for their final two years after high school graduation. This pathway provides a seamless transition to higher education and allows students to begin their college journey early.

How do I apply for enrollment for a new child?

What Graduation Plans are available?

Texas Tech K-12 provides the Foundation Graduation Plan with various endorsement options, allowing students to customize their education based on career interests. The Foundation Plan with Endorsement path offers a well-rounded education, enabling students to graduate with the Distinguished Level of Achievement, which can qualify them for automatic admissions to Texas public universities. Endorsements include:

Step 1: Arts & Humanities

Step 2: Business & Industry

Step 3: Multidisciplinary Studies

Step 4: STEM (Science, Technology, Engineering, Math)

Step 5: Public Services

Each endorsement requires specific advanced coursework in addition to the Foundation Plan core courses, offering students targeted electives and opportunities to develop specialized skills.

Step 1: Allow students to start with Texas Tech K-12 at anytime

Step 8: Recover Credits: Retake courses to make up failed credits and stay on track for graduation.

Single Diploma

The Single Diploma track is for students who want to complete all their high school education through Texas Tech K-12 and earn a Texas high school diploma.

Step 1: Students use Texas Tech K-12 curriculum entirely through online courses.

**Testing Information for TTU K-12**

**Where to Take Tests:**
- The testing department will register you at an approved testing site closest to your home address.
- If the assigned site is not convenient, you may arrange for a local school to host your test. Confirmation from the school is needed 30 days before the testing window starts.
- For students outside Texas, an approved proctor must be found to administer the tests. Contact your testing coordinator for assistance.

**Test Day Requirements:**
- A Texas Tech K-12 student ID is required. Contact your advisor if you don't have one.
- Electronics like cell phones and smartwatches are not allowed and must be handed over to the test administrator.
- You may bring a water bottle, snack, and/or lunch.
- Dress appropriately for the test.

**Online Proctoring:**
- Proctorio is used for online proctoring of final exams and Credit By Exams (CBEs), providing live-authentication and monitoring.
- Exceptions to online proctoring must be approved by a Texas Tech K-12 administrator.

**Preparation and Study Resources:**
- Test preparation materials are available on the Texas Education Agency’s Texas Assessment site: [Texas Assessment](https://www.texasassessment.gov/).
- Steps to access practice tests include selecting "Students and Families," navigating to "Practice Tests Login," and following the prompts to begin practice tests.

**Contact Information:**
- For more information or assistance, contact the TTU K-12 testing coordinator at ttuk12@ttu.edu or call 1-800-692-6877.

query.raw: When can I enroll my child?

chunks.text:
Can my child start at any time during the year?

Yes! Enrollment is available year-round, and students can begin courses at any time. The program's flexible schedule allows students to start when it's convenient for them.

How do I add a child who is already enrolled?

For those that have clicked on "I would like to Add a Child who is already enrolled", the following screen will appear. Please note that if your child is already enrolled, enter their student ID and date of birth to connect them to your account.

Upon entering your student's ID and date of birth, their name should appear under "Students"

How do I apply for enrollment for a new child?

For those that clicked on "I would like to Apply for Enrollment for a new child", the application will appear. Please note that Texas Tech K-12 offers several different programs (each program is listed below). Based upon the selection, application requirements may be different:

Step 1: Texas Tech K-12 Supplemental Program (opens in new tab) - If you remain enrolled at your local school, you must obtain prior approval from your school counselor before enrolling in any course or Credit By Exam. Failure to obtain approval may result in un-awarded credit for a course or Credit By Exam. With prior approval, students enrolled in another school may enroll in:

Step 2: "Supplemental courses (opens in new tab)," and/or

Step 3: Credit-by-Examinations (opens in new tab)," or CBE's.

Step 4: Full-Time Texas Tech K-12 Student (opens in new tab) - If you are withdrawing from your local school district and wish to become a Full-Time Student at Texas Tech K-12, you may apply to:

Step 5: The "Tuition-Free Full-Time Program (opens in new tab)" (Texas Residents), or

Step 6: The "Tuition-Paid Full-Time Program (opens in new tab)" (Outside of Texas or Texas Residents seeking more flexibility).

Step 7: College Preparatory Academy (opens in new tab) - Texas Tech K-12 Full-Time students that may earn both high school and college credit simultaneously. These courses are typically offered through partnerships between high schools and colleges or universities, enabling students to get a head start on their college education while still in high school.

Upon getting to the bottom of the page, you will be presented with the following screen. Parents that are registering their students for the Texas Tech K-12 Supplemental Program or Texas Tech K-12 Full-Time Diploma program should select the "Texas Tech K-12 Intake Form".

I already have a Parent Portal account — how do I add a child?

If you do have an existing account, please click on "I have an Account Registered on the Parent Portal but would like to Add a Child" (opens in new tab). Please note students and parents must have a different email address.

The Parent Portal Registration Page will ask you to enter in your First Name, Last Name and email address. You will also be asked to create a unique password. Please note that the password must be twelve characters in length, and include an upper case, lower case, a number and special character.

Upon entering your information, you will be directed to the "Students" page. From the Students page, you may connect to an existing student(s) account via "I would like to Add a Child who is already enrolled", or you may create an application via "I would like to Apply For Enrollment for a new child".

Tuition-Free Course Enrollment Dates

Step 1: April 5, 2027 - April 16, 2027: Grades 3-8 Reading Language Arts

Step 2: April 12, 2027 - April 23, 2027: Grade 5 Science, Grade 8 Science, Grade 8 Social Studies

Step 2: Lottery Notification: Applications are evaluated upon submission for placement on the lottery waitlist. Applicants will be notified of their status via email.

Step 3: Tuition-Paid Programs: Enrollments for tuition-paid programs can occur at any time as long as space is available.

What do I need to apply?

Step 1: The program must meet your child’s academic needs.

Step 2: Your child needs a computer with the required specs and reliable internet.

Can students with Individualized Education Program (IEPs) or 504 plans enroll?

How is attendance tracked in an online school?

Step 1: Attendance is based on progress in your child’s courses.

Step 2: Your child must complete 5% of each course's assignments each week. For example, if a course has 20 assignments, at least one should be completed each week.

Understanding the Texas Success Initiative Assessment Test

The current Texas Success Initiative Assessment test is version two, commonly referred to as Texas Success Initiative Assessment 2. Step 2: The Texas Success Initiative Assessment in Reading contains multiple choice with approximately 24 questions in the placement test and 10-12 items in each section of the diagnostic test.

Step 3: The Texas Success Initiative Assessment in Writing contains a multiple-choice section and an essay section. There are approximately 24 items in the placement test and 10-12 items per section in the diagnostic test. For the essay section, students are asked to write a five-paragraph essay on an issue of current interest.

What scores do I need to pass?

The minimum passing standards for the Texas Success Initiative Assessment 2 require a College Readiness Classification (CRC) score of at least 950 or a College Readiness Classification score below 950 and a diagnostic level of 6 for Mathematics. A College Readiness Classification score of at least 945 and an essay score of at least 5, or a College Readiness Classification score below 945 and a diagnostic level of 5 or 6, and an essay score of at least 5 are required for the English Language Arts Reading (ELAR) test.

For students who took the original Texas Success Initiative Assessment, the standards are slightly different and require a score of 351 or higher on Reading, a score of 340 or higher and an essay score of 4 or higher for Writing, and a score of 350 or higher for Math.

Understanding the Texas Success Initiative Assessment Test

The current Texas Success Initiative Assessment test is version two, commonly referred to as Texas Success Initiative Assessment 2. Texas Success Initiative Assessment 2 was administered for any student taking the test after Jan. 11, 2021, and replaced the original Texas Success Initiative Assessment test (TSIA).

Before taking Texas Success Initiative Assessment 2, students are required to participate in a Pre-Assessment Activity (opens in new tab). The activity will explain some of the test procedures and provide practice test questions along with feedback on answers to the practice questions. The activity also will provide options and campus resources to help them meet minimum standards.

Step 1: The Texas Success Initiative Assessment in Mathematics contains a multiple-choice assessment with approximately 20 items on the placement test and 10 items in each section of the diagnostic test. Students with passing scores on the placement test will not be required to take the diagnostic test.

Step 2: The Texas Success Initiative Assessment in Reading contains multiple choice with approximately 24 questions in the placement test and 10-12 items in each section of the diagnostic test.

Understanding the Texas Success Initiative Assessment Test

The current Texas Success Initiative Assessment test is version two, commonly referred to as Texas Success Initiative Assessment 2. Texas Success Initiative Assessment 2 was administered for any student taking the test after Jan. 11, 2021, and replaced the original Texas Success Initiative Assessment test (TSIA).

Before taking Texas Success Initiative Assessment 2, students are required to participate in a Pre-Assessment Activity (opens in new tab). The activity will explain some of the test procedures and provide practice test questions along with feedback on answers to the practice questions. The activity also will provide options and campus resources to help them meet minimum standards.

Step 1: The Texas Success Initiative Assessment in Mathematics contains a multiple-choice assessment with approximately 20 items on the placement test and 10 items in each section of the diagnostic test. Students with passing scores on the placement test will not be required to take the diagnostic test.

Step 2: The Texas Success Initiative Assessment in Reading contains multiple choice with approximately 24 questions in the placement test and 10-12 items in each section of the diagnostic test.

Step 3: The Texas Success Initiative Assessment in Writing contains a multiple-choice section and an essay section. There are approximately 24 items in the placement test and 10-12 items per section in the diagnostic test. For the essay section, students are asked to write a five-paragraph essay on an issue of current interest.

Please contact the Texas Tech K 12 testing coordinator (opens in new tab) for student specific requirements or more information. Parents/students should receive information via email in January for Spring State of Texas Assessment of Academic Readiness (STAAR) 6-8 administration. Additional information may be found at State of Texas Assessment of Academic Readiness (STAAR) Testing (opens in new tab).

Texas law (HB 4545 /1416) states that any student who did not pass a State of Texas Assessment of Academic Readiness (STAAR) exam the previous year is REQUIRED to receive 15-30 hours of additional remedial instruction in that content area per year. Failure to attend synchronous tutoring sessions that will be scheduled by the school is a violation of the attendance policy and students will need to return to their local, geographical public school.

Q: How does only ranking the Top 10% benefit students in the top quarter of students who are very close to the Top 10%?

When a student does not have a rank, a college will conduct a holistic review of the student's college application, examining the rigor of courses taken, grades received, SAT/ACT scores, and other factors. This is beneficial to Texas Tech K-12 students just outside the Top 10% because these students, along with many other districts' students, have high grades, high test scores, and strong academic and extra-curricular achievement. Many colleges generate a rank based on these factors. School counselors of other high performing schools that do not rank, report the college assigned rank tends to be higher than the high school generated rank would have been.

Why Texas Tech K-12?

Texas Tech K-12 is fully accredited by the Texas Education Agency (TEA) and approved by the National Collegiate Athletic Association (NCAA). We provide the same rigorous academic standards as traditional schools, but with the flexibility to learn from anywhere at any time. Our online programs cover elementary, middle and high school, and we offer tailored options for individual students as well as entire classes or cohorts.

Will dual credit courses affect my high school Grade Point Average and college transcript?

Yes, dual credit courses can affect both your high school GPA and college transcript. The grades you earn in dual credit courses will typically be recorded on both your high school transcript and your college transcript. This means that your performance in these courses will impact both your high school GPA and your college GPA. It's important to perform well in dual credit courses to maintain a strong academic record for both your high school and college pursuits.

Q: How does this impact admissions to universities?

In high performing school districts like Texas Tech K-12, students who rank outside of the top 10% would normally rank very high at other districts. This can hurt our students in college admissions. If a student has been given a rank by a high school, for example, the 40th percentile, many universities will use that rank as a shortcut to evaluate the student and say that student falls in the top 40% of all applicants to the university. However, if the student does not have a high school rank, the university will evaluate the student's record and assign them a rank relative to other applicants.When compared to other college applicants, our students tend to be more qualified than those who graduate with a similar ranking at other high schools. According to other Texas districts, schools saw a 38% increase in acceptance to the University of Texas and a 49% increase to Texas A&M after eliminating class rank.

My child has an Individualized Education Program (or 504 plan). May he/she enroll in your school?

Online instruction presents different challenges than those in a traditional classroom. The curriculum is rigorous and is reading- and writing-intensive. Successful online students are able to take initiative and manage their own time.

Nevertheless, Texas Tech K-12 strives to offer exceptional education programs that meet the needs of students with disabilities. To qualify, the student's Individual Education Plan (IEP) needs to indicate that the Texas Tech K-12 online program is the appropriate instructional setting for the student and is the student’s least restrictive environment.

The student’s admission, review, and dismissal (ARD) committee has the responsibility of determining whether or not an electronic (online) course/program will meet the needs of a student with a disability. The committee will also take into account the nature of the asynchronous program and what services can be implemented online. It is crucial to note that the program is fully online, providing only services that can be provided virtually as the school does not have a physical location. answer.text:
**Credit By Examination (CBE) Requirements**

- **Without Prior Instruction**: A score of 80% or higher is required. This higher threshold ensures that students demonstrate a strong understanding of the material, as they have not received formal instruction in the subject. It confirms their proficiency and readiness to advance without the foundational teaching typically provided in a classroom setting.

- **With Prior Instruction**: A score of 70% or higher is sufficient. This lower requirement reflects that the student has already received instruction in the subject, and the score indicates a satisfactory level of understanding based on the prior teaching they have received.

The distinction in scoring requirements ensures that students without prior instruction are adequately prepared to progress in their studies independently.

Texas Tech K-12 Elementary School Program Requirements

Texas Tech Elementary School: As a full-time Texas Tech K-12 elementary student, you must maintain academic progress in a minimum of four courses concurrently.

After you complete both first (A) and second (B) semesters of all four core subject areas in your grade level, you will receive a report card. Upon successful completion of these four core subject areas, you will be promoted to the next grade level.

In accordance with Texas Education Code §25.001, children must be 5 years old on or before September 1 of the school year to enroll in Kindergarten. Children who turn 5 after September 1 are not eligible for Kindergarten enrollment. This includes part-time or supplemental enrollment and applies to all programs and enrollments.

Kindergarten Acceleration

The Board has approved the following criterion to allow a child who is five years old on or before September 1 to be assigned initially to grade 1 rather than to kindergarten:

A score of 80 percent or higher on the Texas Tech K-12 Kindergarten Credit by Exam (CBE) via a secured proctor in each of the core areas of English language arts, mathematics, science, and social studies.

Additional criteria for acceleration may include:

Step 1: A letter of recommendation from the preschool or kindergarten class the student has attended;

Step 2: Successful completion in the first discussion-based (DBA) of first grade;

Step 3: Written parental approval.

If it is found to be in the best interest of the student’s academic and affective needs, the Advisor and Principal may make a recommendation to the Superintendent or designee for course or grade-level acceleration. The student’s parents shall be notified by letter of the approval or denial of student acceleration.

Characteristics Related to Potential Giftedness

Step 4: Student’s use of quantitative expressions and quantitative reasoning. An example to illustrate this comes from the writer’s experience in observing a kindergarten class where the students were playing a game in which each round resulted in the elimination of one child. After the game had progressed for several rounds, the teacher asked the children, “Are there more girls left in the game or more boys?” One child responded, “There are only one-half as many boys left as girls.” Not only was the response correct, it was also a highly unusual quantitative response for a kindergarten child to make. Some children exhibit the ability to translate rather lengthy, sometimes complex, verbal material into quantitative terms. The ability to do this kind of translation requires a level of abstraction and facility with quantitative expression that is important to identify.

Step 5: Student’s ability to devise or adopt a systematic strategy for solving problems and to change the strategy if it is not working. This ability discriminates between excellent problem-solvers and average problem-solvers. Children who are exceptional in cognitive development tend to have mastery of a large number of strategies for attacking novel or difficult problems and tend to be able to evaluate the effectiveness of the strategy as they work on the problems and change strategies when the one they are using does not appear to be working. Other children either have no systematic strategy or only one strategy, which they persist in using, even though it should be apparent to them that it is not working.

Step 6: Special skills students exhibit that are unusual for their age or grade. The first five categories listed relate primarily to verbal, quantitative, or problem-solving skills. For example, the writer saw a first-grade child during a free activity period drawing in perspective, which is quite unusual for a child that age. **Full-Time Tuition-Free Diploma Program (TX Residents Only)**

The Full-Time Tuition-Free Diploma Program is available to Texas residents and is funded by the State of Texas. This program provides a K-12 online academic experience without tuition costs for eligible students.

**Requirements to Apply:**

- **Academic Needs:** The program must align with the student's academic needs.
- **Residency:** Applicants must be Texas residents under the age of 25.
- **Proof of Residency:** Submit proof of Texas residency.
- **Birth Certificate:** Provide a copy of the student's birth certificate.
- **Course Enrollment:** Students must be scheduled into at least four semester courses and maintain satisfactory course progress.
- **STAAR/EOC Exams:** Participation in the State of Texas Assessments of Academic Readiness (STAAR) and End of Course (EOC) exams is required for the student's grade level.
- **Learning Coach:** A designated Learning Coach, such as a parent or guardian, is required to assist with monitoring progress and lesson mastery.

**How Students Are Selected:**

- **Application Process:** Students must complete an intake form and submit the required documents, including proof of residency and a birth certificate.
- **Academic Performance:** Satisfactory performance on STAAR assessments is considered, although not mandatory for application.
- **Course Progress:** Students must maintain satisfactory progress in their enrolled courses.

For more information, you can contact TTU K-12 at 1-800-692-6877 or email ttuk12@ttu.edu.

**Full-Time Tuition-Paid Program Overview**

The Full-Time Tuition-Paid Program at Texas Tech K-12 offers a flexible, self-paced online learning environment for students who desire the flexibility of distance education. This program is available to students regardless of residency and is ideal for those who do not meet the eligibility criteria for the tuition-free program, live outside of Texas, or prefer a paid, flexible online learning experience.

**Program Features:**
- **Flexible Learning:** Students can progress at their own pace without attending live classes at specific times.
- **Course Offerings:** Includes core subjects, electives, foreign languages, Advanced Placement (AP) courses, and options for credit recovery and acceleration.
- **Support:** Students receive guidance from certified teachers, access to academic advisers and counselors, and technical support.

**Requirements for Enrollment:**
- **Application Submission:** Complete the online application form and submit required documents such as a birth certificate and previous transcripts.
- **Admission Fee:** A non-refundable $200.00 admission fee is required.
- **Course Enrollment:** Students must be scheduled into at least four semester courses and maintain satisfactory course progress.
- **Technology Access:** Students must have access to a computer with the required specifications and reliable internet.

**Selection Process:**
- **Application Review:** Applications are reviewed to ensure they meet the program's academic needs and requirements.
- **Confirmation:** Once accepted, students receive confirmation of their enrollment and can begin selecting courses with an academic adviser.

For more detailed information on the Full-Time Tuition-Paid Program, including specific course offerings and additional support services, you can contact TTU K-12 at 1-800-692-6877 or email ttuk12@ttu.edu.

Our Texas Tech K-12 Supplemental Program (opens in new tab) is designed to allow students in elementary, middle and high school that allows students to work at their own pace. We have students who must do their work at home for various reasons, such as travel "outside" of the U.S. for extended amounts of time, have health issues, are actors, entertainers, and athletes who cannot fit the traditional schooling into their schedule. We have school all year and do not keep a traditional academic schedule, so it is possible to move through our program faster than the typical semester-based programs.

This is a self-paced program where all the instructional content is provided. The courses tend to be reading and writing intensive. Online courses require self-discipline and excellent time-management skills. The courses are not virtual classrooms and do not require any interaction with any other students or instructors. Each course has lessons, which are like chapters, and a final exam. The final exam will be proctored online by an online proctoring service.

Texas Tech K-12 Elementary School Program Requirements

Texas Tech Elementary School: As a full-time Texas Tech K-12 elementary student, you must maintain academic progress in a minimum of four courses concurrently.

After you complete both first (A) and second (B) semesters of all four core subject areas in your grade level, you will receive a report card. Upon successful completion of these four core subject areas, you will be promoted to the next grade level.

In accordance with Texas Education Code §25.001, children must be 5 years old on or before September 1 of the school year to enroll in Kindergarten. Children who turn 5 after September 1 are not eligible for Kindergarten enrollment. This includes part-time or supplemental enrollment and applies to all programs and enrollments.

answer.text:
**Supplemental Part-Time Program Overview**

The Texas Tech K-12 Supplemental Part-Time Program is designed for students who are enrolled at their local school but wish to take additional courses through Texas Tech K-12. This program is ideal for students who want to:

- Graduate early or on time
- Take courses not offered at their local school
- Make up failed credits
- Have an alternative for summer school

**Requirements**

- **Prior Approval:** Students must receive prior approval from their school counselor before enrolling in any course or Credit By Exam (CBE). Failure to obtain approval may result in unawarded credit.
- **Self-Paced Learning:** The program is self-paced, allowing students to work at their own speed. Courses are reading and writing intensive and require self-discipline and excellent time-management skills.
- **Proctored Exams:** Final exams are proctored online by an online proctoring service.

**Selection Process**

- **Counselor Approval:** Students must obtain approval from their school counselor to ensure the courses align with their academic goals and requirements.
- **Enrollment:** Once approved, students can enroll in the supplemental courses or Credit By Examinations (CBEs).

**Additional Information**

- Students have six months (180 days) from the date of enrollment to complete each course.
- The program offers flexibility for students with unique schedules, such as those who travel, have health issues, or are involved in activities like acting or sports.

For more detailed information or specific inquiries, you can contact TTU K-12 at 1-800-692-6877 or email ttuk12@ttu.edu.

To organize the steps for ordering and processing exams through Texas Tech K-12, follow this sequence:

1. **Order Placement:**
   - For Print Credit By Exams: Complete the Institutional Testing Services Enrollment Form. If ordering for multiple campuses, submit a Test Summary Form for each campus.
   - For Online Credit By Exams: Complete the online order spreadsheet and submit it via the portal. Include the Credit By Exam name, semester, Purchase Order (PO) number or payment tracking ID, and test date.

2. **Processing Times:**
   - Small Orders (1–50 exams): Submit 2 weeks before the test date. Processed within 2 business days.
   - Medium Orders (51–100 exams): Submit 3 weeks before. Processed within 3 business days.
   - Large Orders (100+ exams): Submit 1 month before. Processed within 5–7 business days.

3. **Payment:**
   - Ensure payments and completed forms are received before processing orders. Payments can be made via purchase orders, credit cards, or checks.

4. **Exam Rules & Identification:**
   - Proctorio is required for online proctored exams.
   - Students must show one valid photo ID before testing (e.g., state ID, driver’s license, school ID, passport, yearbook photo with name, or a labeled school photo in the student file).

5. **Order Completion:**
   - District-proctored online Credit By Exam passwords are emailed after orders are processed.

This sequence ensures that all necessary steps are followed for ordering and processing exams efficiently.

How do I enroll in the Full-Time Tuition-Paid Program?

To enroll, follow these steps:

Step 1: Submit an Application: Complete the online application form and submit required documents (e.g., birth certificate and previous transcripts, if applicable).

Step 2: Confirmation: Once your application is reviewed and accepted, you will receive confirmation of your enrollment.

Step 3: Course Selection: Meet with an academic adviser to choose your courses based on your grade level, academic goals and interests.

Step 4: Begin Learning: After enrollment, students can start their courses at any time and access all online resources.

Tuition-Free Application and Lottery Information

2026 - 2027

If you are applying to Texas Tech K-12's tuition-free program and are a Texas resident, please note that enrollment is limited. State law requires a lottery system to select students for admission each semester. The next lottery will take place on October 29, 2026.

First Semester: Course enrollments open Aug. 3, 2026 with courses starting Aug. 3, 2026. We recommend starting early to maximize success and take breaks. Courses must be completed by Jan. 15, 2027.

Second Semester: For current students, course enrollments open December 16, 2026. For new students, course enrollments will open January 4, 2027. Courses must be completed by June 30, 2027.

Tuition-Free Course Enrollment Dates

Step 1: April 5, 2027 - April 16, 2027: Grades 3-8 Reading Language Arts

Step 2: April 12, 2027 - April 23, 2027: Grade 5 Science, Grade 8 Science, Grade 8 Social Studies

Step 3: April 19, 2027 - April 30, 2027: Grades 3-8 Mathematics

Summer EOC (End of Course Exams):

Step 1: June 14, 2027 -  June 25, 2027: Algebra I, Biology, English I, English II, U.S. History

Please note:

Step 1: Automatic Re-Enrollment: If you are currently enrolled in the tuition-free program, a completed re-enrollment form is required for admission to the next school year. No reapplication is necessary.

Step 2: Lottery Notification: Applications are evaluated upon submission for placement on the lottery waitlist. Applicants will be notified of their status via email.

Why Texas Tech K-12?

Texas Tech K-12 is fully accredited by the Texas Education Agency (TEA) and approved by the National Collegiate Athletic Association (NCAA). **Learning Coach Role in Texas Tech K-12**

A Learning Coach is a designated adult, usually a parent or guardian, who collaborates with teachers to support a student's educational progress in the Texas Tech K-12 program. Their responsibilities include:

- Monitoring the student's progress and lesson mastery.
- Reviewing student work.
- Ensuring the student stays on track with their coursework.

**Requirements for a Learning Coach**

- The Learning Coach must be a responsible adult who can dedicate time to assist the student in their learning process.
- They are essential in the Texas Tech K-12 Tuition-Free Academic Program, helping students meet program requirements and remain engaged.

For further details, you can contact Texas Tech K-12 at 1-800-692-6877 or email ttuk12@ttu.edu.

Texas Tech K-12 Middle School - Full-Time

The Texas Tech K-12 middle school program is an engaging and rigorous program that prepares students by forming the foundation for high school. Students enrolled full-time in middle school will complete all core courses in addition to one year of Fine Arts and one year of Career Exploration.

Supplemental Program Information

Anyone looking to supplement their current school curriculum or home school curriculum can enroll in Texas Tech K-12.  Our Texas Tech K-12 Supplemental Program (opens in new tab) is designed to allow students in elementary, middle and high school that allows students to work at their own pace. We have students who must do their work at home for various reasons, such as travel "outside" of the U.S. for extended amounts of time, have health issues, are actors, entertainers, and athletes who cannot fit the traditional schooling into their schedule. We have school all year and do not keep a traditional academic schedule, so it is possible to move through our program faster than the typical semester-based programs.

This is a self-paced program where all the instructional content is provided. The courses tend to be reading and writing intensive. Online courses require self-discipline and excellent time-management skills. The courses are not virtual classrooms and do not require any interaction with any other students or instructors. Texas Tech High School: As a full-time Texas Tech K-12 high school student, you must maintain academic progress in a minimum of four courses concurrently. Note: you will need to take more than the minimum number of courses to stay on grade level and graduate at your desired time.

To complete and retain admission as a student in Texas Tech High School, you must work with an academic advisor and be enrolled in a minimum of four Texas Tech K-12 courses (dual-credit and Credit By Exam's excluded). Generally, you will complete a total of six to seven credits per year (12-14 courses) and must also pass five State of Texas Assessment and Academic Readiness (STAAR) EOC (End of Course) exams to meet graduation requirements.

To graduate with a Texas Tech High School diploma, you will take at least your last year of high school credits (25%) from Texas Tech K-12. Exceptions will be considered by administration on a case-by-case basis but the last semester (2.5 credits) must be taken from Texas Tech K-12.

In addition to working towards a high school diploma, you may request a Verification Of Enrollment and Student ID (opens in new tab) cards. You may also participate in PSAT, ACT, AND SAT exams.

Q: How does this impact admissions to universities?

In high performing school districts like Texas Tech K-12, students who rank outside of the top 10% would normally rank very high at other districts. This can hurt our students in college admissions. If a student has been given a rank by a high school, for example, the 40th percentile, many universities will use that rank as a shortcut to evaluate the student and say that student falls in the top 40% of all applicants to the university. However, if the student does not have a high school rank, the university will evaluate the student's record and assign them a rank relative to other applicants.When compared to other college applicants, our students tend to be more qualified than those who graduate with a similar ranking at other high schools. According to other Texas districts, schools saw a 38% increase in acceptance to the University of Texas and a 49% increase to Texas A&M after eliminating class rank.

Q: How does this impact admissions to universities?

In high performing school districts like Texas Tech K-12, students who rank outside of the top 10% would normally rank very high at other districts. This can hurt our students in college admissions. If a student has been given a rank by a high school, for example, the 40th percentile, many universities will use that rank as a shortcut to evaluate the student and say that student falls in the top 40% of all applicants to the university. However, if the student does not have a high school rank, the university will evaluate the student's record and assign them a rank relative to other applicants.When compared to other college applicants, our students tend to be more qualified than those who graduate with a similar ranking at other high schools. According to other Texas districts, schools saw a 38% increase in acceptance to the University of Texas and a 49% increase to Texas A&M after eliminating class rank.

My child has an Individualized Education Program (or 504 plan). May he/she enroll in your school?

Online instruction presents different challenges than those in a traditional classroom. The curriculum is rigorous and is reading- and writing-intensive. Successful online students are able to take initiative and manage their own time.

Nevertheless, Texas Tech K-12 strives to offer exceptional education programs that meet the needs of students with disabilities. To qualify, the student's Individual Education Plan (IEP) needs to indicate that the Texas Tech K-12 online program is the appropriate instructional setting for the student and is the student’s least restrictive environment.

The student’s admission, review, and dismissal (ARD) committee has the responsibility of determining whether or not an electronic (online) course/program will meet the needs of a student with a disability. The committee will also take into account the nature of the asynchronous program and what services can be implemented online. It is crucial to note that the program is fully online, providing only services that can be provided virtually as the school does not have a physical location. In high performing school districts like Texas Tech K-12, students who rank outside of the top 10% would normally rank very high at other districts. This can hurt our students in college admissions. **Troubleshooting Grade Report Access**

If your grade report isn't showing for a completed course, try the following steps:

- **Switch View**: In the Counselor Portal (Focus Student Information System), switch the view to “View Detailed Report.” Once the page refreshes, the grade report should be available.

- **Browser and Extensions**: Ensure you are using Google Chrome and that the Adobe Acrobat extension is enabled. Check that your Adobe settings allow the conversion of the current web page to an Adobe PDF file.

- **Check Timing**: Make sure that five business days have passed since your final course grade was posted, as it can take this long for grades to be recorded.

If you continue to experience issues, you may want to contact Texas Tech K-12 for further assistance. You can reach them at 1-800-692-6877 or via email at ttuk12@ttu.edu.

chunks.text:
Texas Tech High School Program Requirements

Texas Tech High School: As a full-time Texas Tech K-12 high school student, you must maintain academic progress in a minimum of four courses concurrently. Note: you will need to take more than the minimum number of courses to stay on grade level and graduate at your desired time.

To complete and retain admission as a student in Texas Tech High School, you must work with an academic advisor and be enrolled in a minimum of four Texas Tech K-12 courses (dual-credit and Credit By Exam's excluded). Generally, you will complete a total of six to seven credits per year (12-14 courses) and must also pass five State of Texas Assessment and Academic Readiness (STAAR) EOC (End of Course) exams to meet graduation requirements.

To graduate with a Texas Tech High School diploma, you will take at least your last year of high school credits (25%) from Texas Tech K-12. Exceptions will be considered by administration on a case-by-case basis but the last semester (2.5 credits) must be taken from Texas Tech K-12.

In addition to working towards a high school diploma, you may request a Verification Of Enrollment and Student ID (opens in new tab) cards. You may also participate in PSAT, ACT, AND SAT exams.

Commencement

Texas Tech K-12 celebrates graduates from the full-Time Diploma Program each year during the traditional graduation season. A schedule for upcoming graduation ceremonies can be found on the Graduation Preparation page (opens in new tab) on the Texas Tech K-12 website. Graduating seniors should plan to complete their coursework and final exams at least two weeks in advance of the graduation date to ensure they are included in their desired graduating class. Texas Tech K-12 Full-Time Diploma Program offers class rings, invitations, and caps and gowns through Herff Jones Company (opens in new tab) –

West Texas Graduation Services (opens in new tab).

Contact them by phone at +1-806-744-7337, by fax to +1-806-744-1744, by email to info@westtexasgrad.com (opens in new tab).

I would like to enroll in the Texas Tech High School Diploma Program

If you are interested in enrolling in the Texas Tech K-12 program, we ask that you please complete the intake form (opens in new tab). In the application page, we ask that you please select "Texas Tech K-12 Intake Form" (TTU K-12 Intake Form). On page 2 of the application you will be asked to select the most appropriate program for your student:

Full-time Tuition-Free Diploma Program (TX Residents Only) (opens in new tab)

The State of Texas has designated Texas Tech K-12 eligible to receive state funds. As a result, beginning in August 2021, we will offer a tuition-free K-12 online academic program available only to Texas Residents!  *Note: There are requirements (opens in new tab) to which you must adhere if you wish to be included in the tuition-free program. You will need to withdraw from your local school district to attend Texas Tech K-12 full-time tuition-free program.

Please read carefully: To apply to this program:

Step 1: it must be consistent with your academic needs,

Step 2: you must be a Texas resident under the age of 25 and provide Proof of Residency (opens in new tab),

Can my child earn a diploma through the Full-Time Tuition-Paid Program?

Yes! Upon successful completion of the required coursework, students will receive a Texas Tech K-12 diploma. The program also offers options for credit recovery and accelerated learning, helping students meet their educational goals.

Endorsements

Endorsements consist of a related series of courses that provide students with in-depth knowledge of a subject area. Read more information about endorsement choices at the Texas Education Agency Graduation Toolkit (opens in new tab)

Step 1: In addition to the 22 credits earned on the Foundation Plan, college-bound students in Texas Tech High School will complete one advanced course credit in math and science and two credits of targeted electives.

Step 2: Each endorsement option offered by Texas Tech K-12 has one to four required electives to meet the endorsement: Currently, Texas Tech K-12 offers the endorsements in Science, Technology, Engineering, and Math, business and industry, arts and humanities, and multidisciplinary studies. Texas Tech K-12 academic advisors will guide you through the endorsement selection process and help you choose an endorsement that best fits your interests and existing credits. You may change your endorsement at any time prior to graduation; however, you should be aware that changes to your endorsement could result in additional required course. See the Personal Graduation Plan Checklist (opens in new tab) for specific courses required for each endorsement.

Step 3: All ninth and 10th graders must select an endorsement. After 10th grade, you may opt for the Foundation Plan only with parental consent.

Please contact a Texas Tech K-12 senior academic advisor via our Support Portal (opens in new tab) for information on graduation plans. For additional graduation requirements, refer to the section on State and National Assessments (opens in a new tab).

Program Selection

Step 3: Submit a birth certificate and proof of Texas residency.

Step 4: Your child must have achieved satisfactory performance on the State of Texas Assessment of Academic Readiness (STAAR) assessments.

Full-time Tuition-based Diploma Program (Outside TX or TX Residents seeking more flexibility) (opens in new tab)

Texas Tech K-12 offers a tuition-based option for students who desire the flexibility of a distance education but reside outside of Texas or do not want the additional restrictions of the tuition-free program. We offer all courses necessary to meet the requirements to complete a Texas high school graduation plan. If you are currently a Texas Tech K-12 student or if you want to withdraw from your local school district to attend Texas Tech K-12 full-time but you do not want the additional restrictions of the tuition-free program, you will select this option. There will be a $200.00 non-refundable Admission fee charged to apply to the Full-time Tuition-based Diploma Program. Once a student submits an assignment for grading, they are no longer eligible for a refund in the tuition-paid or supplemental programs.

College Preparatory Academy (Do not select if you do not meet the criteria listed below) (opens in new tab)

Texas Tech K-12 offers both individual dual credit courses or a comprehensive Texas Tech College Preparatory Academy program. The College Preparatory Academy is designed to help students graduate with both a high school diploma and a bachelor's degree in just six years.

In order to apply for the College Preparatory Academy, you must meet the following criteria:

Step 1: Achieved Mastered State of Texas Assessment of Academic Readiness (STAAR) scores

Step 2: Provided one academic recommendation letter

Step 3: Maintained a 3.0 GPA

Step 4: Enrolled in the Texas Tech K-12 Full-Time Diploma Program

Single Diploma

The Single Diploma track is for students who want to complete all their high school education through Texas Tech K-12 and earn a Texas high school diploma.

Step 1: Students use Texas Tech K-12 curriculum entirely through online courses.

Step 2: This track is best for students with strong English skills due to the rigorous demands of reading, writing, and speaking in English.

Step 3: Ideal for: Students wanting a fully online education with a Texas high school diploma.

**Graduating with TTU K-12 with One Semester Left**

- **Enrollment Requirement**: To graduate with a Texas Tech High School diploma, you must take at least your last year of high school credits (25%) from Texas Tech K-12. Specifically, the last semester (2.5 credits) must be completed through Texas Tech K-12.

Concurrent Diploma

This option allows students to pursue two high school diplomas—one from their local school and one from Texas Tech K-12.

Step 1: Students take a mix of online courses from Texas Tech K-12 and transfer credits from their local school.

Step 2: Students must have adequate English language skills to succeed.

Step 3: Entrance exams help assess academic and English proficiency before admission.

Step 4: Ideal for: Students looking to earn two diplomas simultaneously.

Pricing (Institutional)

Step 1: Online course: $300

Step 2: Online Credit By Exam: $80

Step 3: Print Credit By Exam: $30

Step 4: District-proctored online Credit By Exam: $30

Step 5: District partners get 15% off online courses

Payment rules

Step 1: We accept purchase orders, credit cards, or checks from schools.

Step 2: Payment and forms must arrive before we process the order.

Step 3: All Credit By Exam fees are non-refundable. Print Credit By Exams can be substituted.

How to place an order

Step 1: Print Credit By Exams: complete the Institutional Testing Services Enrollment Form and, if ordering for multiple campuses, submit a Test Summary Form for each campus.

Step 2: Online Credit By Exams: complete the online order spreadsheet and submit it via our portal. Include Credit By Exam name, semester, Purchase Order (PO) number or payment tracking identification (ID), and test date.

Step 3: District-proctored online Credit By Exams: available only for specific courses (e.g., Algebra 1A/B, Biology 1A/B, English 1A/B, Spanish 1A/B, US History 1A/B). Ask us if you are unsure.

Order processing times (recommended submission)

Step 1: Small (1–50 exams): submit 2 weeks before test date. Processed within 2 business days.

Step 2: Medium (51–100): submit 3 weeks before. Processed within 3 business days.

Step 3: Large (100+): submit 1 month before. Processed within 5–7 business days.

Step 4: District-proctored online Credit By Exam passwords are emailed after orders are processed.

Online exam rules & Identification

Step 1: Proctorio is required for online proctored exams.

Step 2: Students must show one valid photo identification (ID) before testing:

Step 3: state identification/driver’s license, school identification, passport, yearbook photo with name, or a labeled school photo in the student file.

Fast Track to Graduation - High School Diploma and Bachelor's Degree in Six Years

Graduate with both a high school diploma and a bachelor's degree in just six years. Imagine starting your career with two credentials in hand, getting a leg up on the competition. With dual credit courses, you'll not only accelerate your academic journey but also gain invaluable insight into college-level expectations, equipping you with the skills and knowledge needed to thrive in higher education and beyond.

High School Credit Courses

Students who receive approval to earn high school credits in Texas Tech High School must successfully complete the corresponding State of Texas Assessment of Academic Readiness End of Course (EOC) exams for Algebra 1, Biology, English 1, English 2, and U.S. History. Students in Texas will test in a local public or charter school. Additional information may be found at State of Texas Assement of Academic Readiness (STAAR) Testing (opens in new tab). Residents outside of Texas: submit a support request (opens in new tab) to assist in testing arrangements.

Required 2026-2027 State of Texas Assessments of Academic Readiness/End of Course Testing Dates:

Step 1: November 30, 2026 – December 11, 2026: Algebra I, Biology, English I, English II, U.S. History

TELEPAS (Texas English Language Proficiency Assessment System):

Step 1: February 15, 2027 - March 26, 2027

Spring EOC (End of Course Exams):

Step 1: April 5, 2027 -  April 16, 2027: English I, English II

Step 2: April 12, 2027 - April 23, 2027: Biology, U.S. History

Step 3: April 19, 2027 - April 30, 2027: Algebra I

Spring STAAR (State of Texas Assessments of Academic Readiness):

Step 1: April 5, 2027 - April 16, 2027: Grades 3-8 Reading Language Arts

Step 2: April 12, 2027 - April 23, 2027: Grade 5 Science, Grade 8 Science, Grade 8 Social Studies

Step 3: April 19, 2027 - April 30, 2027: Grades 3-8 Mathematics

Summer EOC (End of Course Exams):

Step 1: June 14, 2027 -  June 25, 2027: Algebra I, Biology, English I, English II, U.S. History

All students following the Foundation Graduation Plan with Endorsement complete a total of 26 credits, encompassing core subjects and electives. Credit requirements include:

**Including one-half credit of communications and speech

If you enrolled in ninth grade before the 2014-15 school year, you must complete the 26-credit Recommended High School Program (RHSP) or the 22-credit Minimum High School Program (MHSP), and you must meet the state testing requirements for your graduation plan.

How do I apply for enrollment for a new child?

For those that clicked on "I would like to Apply for Enrollment for a new child", the application will appear. Please note that Texas Tech K-12 offers several different programs (each program is listed below). Based upon the selection, application requirements may be different:

Step 1: Texas Tech K-12 Supplemental Program (opens in new tab) - If you remain enrolled at your local school, you must obtain prior approval from your school counselor before enrolling in any course or Credit By Exam. Failure to obtain approval may result in un-awarded credit for a course or Credit By Exam. With prior approval, students enrolled in another school may enroll in:

Step 2: "Supplemental courses (opens in new tab)," and/or

Step 3: Credit-by-Examinations (opens in new tab)," or CBE's.

Step 4: Full-Time Texas Tech K-12 Student (opens in new tab) - If you are withdrawing from your local school district and wish to become a Full-Time Student at Texas Tech K-12, you may apply to:

Step 5: The "Tuition-Free Full-Time Program (opens in new tab)" (Texas Residents), or

Step 6: The "Tuition-Paid Full-Time Program (opens in new tab)" (Outside of Texas or Texas Residents seeking more flexibility).

Step 7: College Preparatory Academy (opens in new tab) - Texas Tech K-12 Full-Time students that may earn both high school and college credit simultaneously. These courses are typically offered through partnerships between high schools and colleges or universities, enabling students to get a head start on their college education while still in high school.

Upon getting to the bottom of the page, you will be presented with the following screen. Parents that are registering their students for the Texas Tech K-12 Supplemental Program or Texas Tech K-12 Full-Time Diploma program should select the "Texas Tech K-12 Intake Form".

Do you offer Dual Credit?

You must contact your advisor for approval of dual credit enrollment.

ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE (AI) USE POLICY (REVISED 2025)

This policy covers any generative Artificial Intelligence tool, such as Chat Generative Pre-trained Transformer, Elicit, Photo Math, etc. This includes text and artwork/graphics/video/audio, etc.

All work submitted in this course must be your own. You may not use artificial intelligence tools to complete your assignments in this course.

If an instructor suspects that an assignment is not the work of the student, it will receive a score of zero. The instructor will message the student or provide feedback on the assignment indicating the need to schedule a one-on-one video conference, during which the student will be required to demonstrate their skills or knowledge through an alternative or mutually agreed-upon assignment. The grade of the alternate or agreed upon assignment will be determined at the instructor’s discretion with the highest possible score being 70%.

If it is determined that a student has violated final exam directions on Final Exam A or Credit By Exam Set 1, the exam will be scored as zero. The student may take Final Exam B or Credit By Exam Set 2 with the highest possible score being 70%.

The incident will be reported to Texas Tech K-12 Administration and documented in the student’s file. Continued violations of Texas Tech University’s Academic Integrity Policy will result in the removal of the student from the program. Texas Tech Student Handbook (opens in new tab)

I would like to enroll in the Texas Tech K-12 Dual Credit Program

Becoming a Texas Tech K-12 student is easy and offers numerous benefits: graduate on time or early, make up failed credits, take courses not offered in your school, earn credits during the summer without attending traditional summer school, supplement your school or homeschool curriculum, and work at a pace that's right for you.  To get started, please complete the "intake form (opens in new tab)". In the form type, please select "College Preparatory Academy".

According to the Texas Administrative Code (TAC)

Step 1: Texas Administrative Code §74.24(b)(2): Students in grades K-5 may take a Credit By Exam for grade acceleration. They must meet an 80% passing standard to be accelerated a grade.

Step 2: Texas Administrative Code §74.24(c)(8)(C): Students in grades 6-12 may take a Credit By Exam for course credit. They must meet an 80% passing standard if they have received no prior instruction.

Step 3: Texas Administrative Code §74.24(c)(12): Students in grades 6-12 may take a Credit By Exam for course credit. They must meet a 70% passing standard if they have received prior instruction.

Step 4: Texas Administrative Code §74.24(c)(9): Students are allowed a maximum of two attempts per Credit By Exam for a specific high school course.

Pathway to Success - Earn Credits Before Graduation

Earning dual credit in high school offers several benefits, especially through online dual credit courses like those offered by Texas Tech K-12. Students can complete their initial two years of undergraduate studies at Texas Tech K-12 before transitioning to Texas Tech for their final two years after high school graduation. This pathway provides a seamless transition to higher education and allows students to begin their college journey early.

To take a single course, students do not need to withdraw from their current school. Students need to obtain approval from their current school Counselor or Principal before enrolling. Students should coordinate with their school Counselor concerning their local school policies and other requirements.

Asynchronous Enrollment:

Students can enroll in courses and Credit by Exams (CBEs) year-round, without enrollment deadlines, making it easy to:

Step 1: Stay on track to graduate on time or early.

Step 2: Recover credits from failed courses.

Step 3: Earn credits during the summer.

Step 4: Access courses not offered at your school.

Step 5: Test out of subjects through Credit By Exams.

Recommend our online high school diploma program to students struggling in traditional settings. Students transfer to Texas Tech K-12 to complete courses at their own pace, all while being counted as transfers—not dropouts—on district records.

Online exam rules & Identification

Step 2: Use Google Chrome for proctored exams.

Step 3: Enable JavaScript and cookies. Turn off ad blockers. Allow pop-ups.

Step 5: Have your photo identification ready.

Step 6: Run the Proctorio system check before the exam.

Step 2: Google Chrome is required for Proctorio.

Step 3: Latest versions of Chrome, Firefox, Edge, or Safari work for other parts of the system.

Step 4: Internet: at least 1.5 Megabits per second (faster recommended). Wired preferred.

Step 5: Enable JavaScript and cookies; disable ad blockers.

Step 6: Portable Document Format (PDF): download and view with an external PDF reader (like Adobe Acrobat Reader).

Yes, the Full-Time Tuition-Paid Program offers:

Step 1: Credit Recovery: Students who need to recover credits from previous courses can enroll in specific courses to get back on track.

Step 2: Accelerated Learning: Students can take advanced or Advanced Placement courses to accelerate their academic progress and prepare for college or career goals.

Grades 9-12

A student in grades 9-12 may be awarded credit based on performance on a Credit By Exam taken with no prior instruction. Students who have had no prior instruction must be awarded credit for the applicable course if the student receives:

Step 1: A score of 80% or higher on the Credit By Exam assessment,

Step 2: A three or higher on Advanced Placement exam, or

Accredited school transcripts are required upon enrollment and will be reviewed for awarding of credit.

Texas Tech High School Program Requirements

Texas Tech High School: As a full-time Texas Tech K-12 high school student, you must maintain academic progress in a minimum of four courses concurrently. Note: you will need to take more than the minimum number of courses to stay on grade level and graduate at your desired time.

To complete and retain admission as a student in Texas Tech High School, you must work with an academic advisor and be enrolled in a minimum of four Texas Tech K-12 courses (dual-credit and Credit By Exam's excluded). Generally, you will complete a total of six to seven credits per year (12-14 courses) and must also pass five State of Texas Assessment and Academic Readiness (STAAR) EOC (End of Course) exams to meet graduation requirements.

Step 1: Students use Texas Tech K-12 curriculum entirely through online courses.

Step 2: This track is best for students with strong English skills due to the rigorous demands of reading, writing, and speaking in English.

answer.text: To graduate with a Texas Tech High School diploma, you must complete at least your last 2.5 credits through Texas Tech K-12. These credits do not have to be concurrent classes like English 1A and English 1B. It's important to consult with an academic advisor to select the courses that best meet your graduation requirements and personal academic goals. For further assistance, you can contact TTU K-12 at 1-800-692-6877 or email ttuk12@ttu.edu.

Endorsements consist of a related series of courses that provide students with in-depth knowledge of a subject area. Read more information about endorsement choices at the Texas Education Agency Graduation Toolkit (opens in new tab)

Step 1: In addition to the 22 credits earned on the Foundation Plan, college-bound students in Texas Tech High School will complete one advanced course credit in math and science and two credits of targeted electives.

Step 2: Each endorsement option offered by Texas Tech K-12 has one to four required electives to meet the endorsement: Currently, Texas Tech K-12 offers the endorsements in Science, Technology, Engineering, and Math, business and industry, arts and humanities, and multidisciplinary studies. Texas Tech K-12 academic advisors will guide you through the endorsement selection process and help you choose an endorsement that best fits your interests and existing credits. You may change your endorsement at any time prior to graduation; however, you should be aware that changes to your endorsement could result in additional required course. See the Personal Graduation Plan Checklist (opens in new tab) for specific courses required for each endorsement.

Step 3: All ninth and 10th graders must select an endorsement. After 10th grade, you may opt for the Foundation Plan only with parental consent.

Please contact a Texas Tech K-12 senior academic advisor via our Support Portal (opens in new tab) for information on graduation plans. For additional graduation requirements, refer to the section on State and National Assessments (opens in a new tab).

What Graduation Plans are available?

Texas Tech K-12 provides the Foundation Graduation Plan with various endorsement options, allowing students to customize their education based on career interests. The Foundation Plan with Endorsement path offers a well-rounded education, enabling students to graduate with the Distinguished Level of Achievement, which can qualify them for automatic admissions to Texas public universities. Endorsements include:

Step 1: Arts & Humanities

Step 2: Business & Industry

Step 3: Multidisciplinary Studies

Step 4: STEM (Science, Technology, Engineering, Math)

Step 5: Public Services

Each endorsement requires specific advanced coursework in addition to the Foundation Plan core courses, offering students targeted electives and opportunities to develop specialized skills.

Foundation Graduation Plan plus Endorsements

If you enrolled in ninth grade during or after the 2014-15 school year, you will graduate under the rules of House Bill 5 (HB 5). HB 5 graduation plans consist of a Foundation Graduation Plan plus one of five endorsements from which students may choose.

Step 2: Electives (art, music, technology, etc.)

Step 3: Foreign languages (Spanish, French, etc.)

Step 4: Advanced Placement (AP) courses

Step 1: First Name

Step 2: Last Name

Step 3: Mailing Address

Step 4: Phone Number

Step 1: Students use Texas Tech K-12 curriculum entirely through online courses.

Step 2: This track is best for students with strong English skills due to the rigorous demands of reading, writing, and speaking in English.

Step 3: Ideal for: Students wanting a fully online education with a Texas high school diploma.

Attendance/Progress Requirements

Step 1: In your all-online program, attendance “will” be defined as progress within each semester course.

Step 2: You will have six months to complete each semester course.

Step 3: You must maintain enrollment in a minimum of four semester courses.

Step 4: You must make weekly progress in each course by working in each course a minimum of three days per 7-day period.

Step 5: You must complete a minimum of 5% of course assignments in every seven-day period. For example, if your course has 20 assignments, you need to complete a minimum of one per week. If your course has 60 assignments, you must average a minimum of three per week.

Please note:

Step 1: Completing the minimum number of assignments does not guaranteed you will complete within the 6-month time frame.

Step 2: Completing the minimum number of assignments and courses may not maintain your appropriate grade level or anticipated graduation date.

Step 3: If your progress is adequate, your parent may request “vacation” days.

Step 4: Extensions are not available, so you must schedule your weekly progress to complete the minimum of four courses during the 6-month period.

Step 5: Failure to meet minimum progress requirements may cause Texas Tech K-12 to implement truancy processes and may result in your removal from the program.

Fast Track to Graduation - High School Diploma and Bachelor's Degree in Six Years

Graduate with both a high school diploma and a bachelor's degree in just six years. Imagine starting your career with two credentials in hand, getting a leg up on the competition. With dual credit courses, you'll not only accelerate your academic journey but also gain invaluable insight into college-level expectations, equipping you with the skills and knowledge needed to thrive in higher education and beyond.

Step 1: Print Credit By Exams: complete the Institutional Testing Services Enrollment Form and, if ordering for multiple campuses, submit a Test Summary Form for each campus.

Step 2: Online Credit By Exams: complete the online order spreadsheet and submit it via our portal. Include Credit By Exam name, semester, Purchase Order (PO) number or payment tracking identification (ID), and test date.

Step 3: District-proctored online Credit By Exams: available only for specific courses (e.g., Algebra 1A/B, Biology 1A/B, English 1A/B, Spanish 1A/B, US History 1A/B). Ask us if you are unsure.

Step 1: Small (1–50 exams): submit 2 weeks before test date. Processed within 2 business days.

Step 2: Medium (51–100): submit 3 weeks before. Processed within 3 business days.

Step 3: Large (100+): submit 1 month before. Processed within 5–7 business days.

**Graduation Credit Requirements for Texas Tech High School**

To graduate with a Texas Tech High School diploma, students must:

- Complete a total of 22 credits on the Foundation Plan.
- Take at least their last year of high school credits (25%) from Texas Tech K-12, with the last semester (2.5 credits) taken from Texas Tech K-12.

**Enrollment for Students with a 504 Plan**

If you are denied a Verification Of Enrollment, your Texas Tech K-12 academic advisor will work with you to outline a progress intervention plan to meet the requirements necessary to receive a Verification Of Enrollment in the future.

**Verification of Enrollment and Attendance (VOE)**

- **Eligibility**: Full-time students at Texas Tech K-12 are eligible to receive a Verification of Enrollment and Attendance (VOE) for purposes such as obtaining a driver’s permit, Social Security benefits, child support, avoiding truancy, or legal documentation of enrollment.

- **Request Process**:
  - Email your Texas Tech K-12 academic advisor to request a Texas Department of Public Safety (DPS) Verification Of Enrollment Form or an official letter verifying enrollment and attendance.
  - The advisor will require at least two working days to review your progress before issuing the verification.

- **Progress Requirements**: Texas Tech K-12 administration may deny verification if a student has not maintained adequate progress to stay on grade level. If denied, the academic advisor will help outline a progress intervention plan to meet the necessary requirements for future verification.

For further assistance, you can contact Texas Tech K-12 at 1-800-692-6877 or email ttuk12@ttu.edu.

A score of 80 percent or higher on the Texas Tech K-12 Kindergarten Credit by Exam (CBE) via a secured proctor in each of the core areas of English language arts, mathematics, science, and social studies.

Additional criteria for acceleration may include:

Step 1: A letter of recommendation from the preschool or kindergarten class the student has attended;

Step 2: Successful completion in the first discussion-based (DBA) of first grade;

Step 3: Written parental approval.

Step 3: Courses must be completed within the designated tuition free program semester timeline.

Step 4: Students must stay enrolled in at least four courses.

How do I apply:

Step 1: New students enter a lottery every six months (fall for the new school year and January for mid-year transfers).

Step 2: If not selected, you’ll be placed on a waitlist and notified if a spot opens.

Texas Tech High School Program Requirements

Texas Tech High School: As a full-time Texas Tech K-12 high school student, you must maintain academic progress in a minimum of four courses concurrently. Note: you will need to take more than the minimum number of courses to stay on grade level and graduate at your desired time.

To complete and retain admission as a student in Texas Tech High School, you must work with an academic advisor and be enrolled in a minimum of four Texas Tech K-12 courses (dual-credit and Credit By Exam's excluded). Generally, you will complete a total of six to seven credits per year (12-14 courses) and must also pass five State of Texas Assessment and Academic Readiness (STAAR) EOC (End of Course) exams to meet graduation requirements.

To graduate with a Texas Tech High School diploma, you will take at least your last year of high school credits (25%) from Texas Tech K-12. Exceptions will be considered by administration on a case-by-case basis but the last semester (2.5 credits) must be taken from Texas Tech K-12.

We have school all year and do not keep a traditional academic schedule, so it is possible to move through our program faster than the typical semester-based programs.

This is a self-paced program where all the instructional content is provided. The courses tend to be reading and writing intensive.
